idiom_name: Sequelize hasMany with include-on-create + onDelete CASCADE (Mongoose subdocuments)
implementation_notes: With Sequelize the parent's mapper owns the children: Order.hasMany(OrderLine) plus include in Order.create writes the lines in the same transaction, and onDelete: 'CASCADE' lets deleting the parent delete the rows; no OrderLine route, service or repository is exported. In a document store the same mapping is a Mongoose subdocument - the child schema is embedded in the parent, calling save() on the child is documented as a no-op, and only parent.save() persists the change (the parent also runs the child's validation and middleware). Both replace mapper delegation with framework configuration; choose an explicit child model only when another consumer must query the child independently.
pitfalls: onDelete: 'CASCADE' only reaches the database when the association is migrated with that constraint (Sequelize.sync or a migration); hooks: true is the alternative when you want Sequelize-level cascade instead.
include on create/update is easy to forget: a bare OrderLine.create() call bypasses the parent's transaction and recreates the second write path.
Mongoose subdocuments inherit the 16 MB document limit: letting the dependent array grow is an unbounded-document bug, not dependent mapping.
